answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. This is why the network can stay open without a central gatekeeper: the economics of reputation do the filtering that a trusted authority otherwise would. Consider a wander as the anchor of the cost.
